transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
President Trump's campaign sprint to war the midterm elections in three weeks takes him
today to Alaska.
He embarked on the roughly 3,400-mile trip to help Republican Senator Dan Sullivan fend
off a challenge from Democratic former Congresswoman Mary Piltola, whose campaign has emphasized
affordability issues.
Here's NPR's Frank Ordonez.
The president continues to struggle in the polls, but he insists his campaign appearances
are helping Republicans in competitive races.
The White House says Trump's travel schedule will only intensify over the next few weeks,
leading up to the midterms.
He has stops planned in Georgia, Kentucky, and Florida.
The president has focused largely on red states, as the campaign seeks to boost enthusiasm
with his base.
The political strategists warn Trump may actually be dealing more harm for his party by stirring
up opposition, Franco Ordonez and PR News, the White House.
The new White House press secretary, Katie Zachariah, held her first press briefing
today.
One of the top issues, the administration's decision to oust U.S. Ambassador to Greece,
Kimberly Guilfoyle.
We have asked Ambassador Guilfoyle to resign.
She has been a wonderful asset to the team, and we wish her well.
Guilfoyle, who was once engaged to Donald Trump Jr., resigned amid allegations of misconduct
before and during her tenure in Athens.
Cornell University has suspended parties at fraternity houses for the rest of the academic
year, among other changes in response to a student's allegations of gang rape in 2024.
Here's NPR's Alyssa Nedworney.
The university announced a number of changes to strengthen campus safety and better support
sexual assault survivors.
In addition to banning all parties and social events at fraternity houses, the Ivy League
School will also hire staff to help students navigate reporting sexual misconduct and will
hire criminal investigators independent of Cornell to investigate allegations of sexual
assault on campus.
In a letter to the campus, the school's president, Michael Kotlikoff, writes, "Cornell must
be a place where safety is not an open question.
The changes come amid continued frustration and protests from students and faculty on the
handling of Jane Doe's 2024 case."
Alyssa Nedworney, NPR News, Ithaca, New York.
Dwayne Kefi D. Davis is being sentenced to 40 years to life in prison for the 1996 murder
of Tupac Shakur.
Shakur's sister, Situa Shakur, told the Las Vegas courtroom today both of her children
were raised in her grief.
They have trust issues, abandonment issues, relationship issues because the first 10 years
of their lives, I really couldn't get over the loss of one brother, Tupac.
Davis told the court that he plans to appeal.
You're listening to NPR News.
The supermarket chain Kroger says it plans to lay off 3,000 corporate employees because
of AI.
In a memo to staff yesterday, CEO Greg Forran says Kroger needs to, quote, "adopt capabilities
and use the technology to reduce duplicative work."
Forran was an executive at Walmart where he sped up the global retailer's digital capabilities.
He took charge of Kroger earlier this year.
Kroger employs more than 400,000 people and operates more than 2,700 stores under brands
such as Fred Meyer Ralphs and King Supers.
The WNBA has announced that Games 3 and 4 of the finals next week will be rescheduled.
NPR's Becky Sullivan reports a change was needed to accommodate conflicts at Atlanta's
Major Arena.
The Atlanta Dream have swept their way through the playoffs to reach the WNBA finals for
the first time in 13 years where they'll face the Golden State Valkyries.
There was just one problem.
The Dream normally play in a very small arena.
The Gateway Center Arena was built before the league's boom in popularity, and it seats
just 3,500 fans, far too few for the very biggest games of the WNBA season.
Often the Dream moves marquee games to State Farm Arena, home of the NBA team, the Atlanta
Hawks, but there were scheduling conflicts with Games 3 and 4, concert one night, and
the Hawks' home opener the other, a situation critics called "embarrassing and avoidable."
Now the league says Games 3 will be moved up a night, while Game 4 will tip off a few
hours early in the Hawks' game a little later that night to fit both.
Becky Sullivan, NPR News.

topics.text: Trump travels to Alaska to campaign for Senator Dan Sullivan against Mary Peltola
White House says Trump's campaign travel will intensify before midterms, with stops in Georgia, Kentucky, Florida
New White House press secretary Katie Zachariah holds first briefing; administration ousts Ambassador Kimberly Guilfoyle from Greece
Cornell University suspends fraternity house parties and adds safety measures after 2024 gang rape allegations
Dwayne Keith Davis sentenced to 40 years to life for 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur; Shakur's sister speaks in court
Kroger plans to lay off 3,000 corporate employees, citing AI-driven efficiency under CEO Greg Foran
WNBA reschedules Games 3 and 4 of Finals, Atlanta Dream vs. Golden State Valkyries, over arena conflicts
